chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Yazid ibn Khalifah al-Harithi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) disliked the sale of juice (fresh fruit extract) with delayed delivery.

key_terms.كَرِهَ: Disliked (indicating a preferred but not strictly forbidden ruling in fiqh)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on selling fresh fruit juice with delayed delivery in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) expresses dislike (*karahah*) for selling fresh fruit juice (*asir*) with deferred delivery, a specific application of the prohibition of *gharrar* (uncertainty). This ruling addresses the risk of spoilage or quality alteration in perishable goods during the delay period, ensuring fairness in commercial transactions. It reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on minimizing ambiguity in contracts to prevent disputes and injustice.
